voice: male, English, global ear; say 'Tiruppur' slowly
status: DRAFT v2 for AK review, 30 Oct 2026. Not voiced.
format: F10 Paradox (with an F5 own-words layer), Indica Atlas G4 'Why Here?' on the scale ladder

beats.say: This is Tiruppur, a town in south India. The nearest port city is about a hundred and seventy kilometres away.
beats.caption: ≈170 km to Kochi
beats.visual: Satellite night view; a straight-line ruler draws Tiruppur → Kochi while a counter runs 0 → 170 km

beats.say: Its rivers carry water only in the monsoon. And the town had no reliable piped water supply.
beats.caption: Rivers: monsoon only
beats.visual: Dry riverbed (Noyyal) on satellite; empty tap icon

beats.say: And yet, for twenty twenty-five to twenty-six, India's government listed Tiruppur first among five hundred and forty-eight exporting districts, for textiles and clothing.
beats.caption: No. 1 of 548 districts
beats.visual: India map; 548 dots light up, one amber dot rises to the top: Tiruppur. Credit: Ministry of Textiles, PIB, 11 Aug 2026 (DGCIS provisional)

beats.say: No sea. Little water. The top exporting district for textiles and clothing. All three are true. So how?
beats.caption: HOW?
beats.visual: Three stamps on the map: ⚓✕ · 💧 · No. 1; then a single question mark

beats.say: The answer isn't one lucky break. It's a cotton market, a rule that kept businesses small, and a town that built the things geography didn't give it. One piece at a time.
beats.caption: COTTON · SMALL · BUILT
beats.visual: Three cards, face down, flipped one by one

beats.say: Start with the globe. Find India. Now slide down to its far south.
beats.caption: India
beats.visual: Orthographic globe → India; one amber highlight; 1.35 s hand-off to the flat map

beats.say: Tiruppur sits about forty-three kilometres from Coimbatore, in a straight line. Coimbatore is a city of mills. Hold on to that.
beats.caption: ≈43 km · Coimbatore
beats.visual: Ruler draws Tiruppur → Coimbatore (straight line, labelled 'straight line')

beats.say: Tiruppur has been a district of its own only since two thousand and nine, carved out of Coimbatore and Erode.
beats.caption: District since 2009
beats.visual: District outlines split apart (labels only; outline marked 'not official' until Survey of India file)

beats.say: The land is dry. The UN's industry agency, UNIDO, calls it 'a dry-water-scarce region'.
beats.caption: 'dry-water-scarce'
beats.visual: Satellite in summer tones; quote card with small credit 'UNIDO case study'

beats.say: So private tankers pumped groundwater and trucked it in. As the water table fell, the tankers drove further. Up to fifty kilometres.
beats.caption: Tankers: up to 50 km
beats.visual: Animated tanker on a road; odometer ticks to 50 km

beats.say: And the cargo? Goods went out 'through all southern ports and Mumbai'. Exporters 'often missed sailings'.
beats.caption: 'often missed sailings'
beats.visual: Lines fan out from Tiruppur to southern ports and Mumbai; a ship leaves an empty berth

beats.say: So: no port next door, and little water. Nothing on this map says, build an export town here. So why here?
beats.caption: WHY HERE?
beats.visual: Zoom back to the bare map; question mark over Tiruppur

beats.say: Go back to eighteen eighty-seven. A district manual calls Tirupur 'a busy railway station, whence a great deal of cotton is despatched'.
beats.caption: 1887 · cotton
beats.visual: Old manual page (rough sketch); steam train with cotton bales

beats.say: By the nineteen sixties, merchants from mill centres all over India came here in season, to buy a prized local cotton called Cambodia cotton.
beats.caption: Cambodia cotton
beats.visual: Arrows from across India converge on Tiruppur; cotton boll close-up. Credit: Coimbatore District Gazetteer, 1966

beats.say: A study of the Tirupur cotton market counted twenty-six ginning factories. Those are the machines that pull the seed out of cotton.
beats.caption: 26 ginning factories
beats.visual: Name the part (T11): seed, fibre, gin; 26 small factory icons fill the town

beats.say: And next door, Coimbatore had forty-two yarn and textile mills, the same study says.
beats.caption: 42 mills next door
beats.visual: Coimbatore lights up with 42 mill icons; yarn lines run to Tiruppur

beats.say: So Tiruppur had cotton coming in, and yarn being spun next door. UNIDO lists that yarn from Coimbatore's mills as one reason the town grew, along with farm crops that failed.
beats.caption: COTTON + YARN
beats.visual: Card 1 flips: COTTON

beats.say: So when did the first knitting unit open? Ask three sources, and you get three dates. Nineteen twenty-five, nineteen thirty-five, and nineteen thirty-seven.
beats.visual: Three source cards (TEA · Textile Commissioner · UNIDO), each with its own date

beats.say: A union leader's account says it began with two friends, one small unit, making banians, that is, vests, for the local market.
beats.caption: Banian = vest
beats.visual: Hand-cranked machine and a white vest only; no faces (dossier §8)

beats.say: In that account, one of the two friends was Hindu and the other was Muslim.
beats.visual: Two hands on one machine; no faces, no religious symbols
beats.ak_check: t21: founders' religion (rule 4.4). One person's 2004 account; adds warmth but is sensitive. AK decides.

beats.say: Here's the odd part. In the official district gazetteer of nineteen sixty-six, Tiruppur is still a cotton town. Knitting barely gets a line.
beats.caption: 1966: still a cotton town
beats.visual: Gazetteer page; the word 'knitting' found once, tiny

beats.say: So how does a cotton town end up with thousands of knitting units? The answer starts with a law.
beats.caption: A LAW
beats.visual: Gavel icon over the cotton map

beats.say: In the early nineteen sixties, a law reserved cotton hosiery knitting for small and cottage units.
beats.caption: Small units only
beats.visual: One big factory icon fades; small workshop icons appear

beats.say: So anyone with more money did the obvious thing. They split the work into two or three smaller units.
beats.caption: 1 → 2 or 3
beats.visual: One workshop splits into three

beats.say: Then, in nineteen seventy-two, an excise duty discouraged making a unit bigger. So firms opened new units instead, often in the same building.
beats.caption: 1972 excise duty
beats.visual: Three nameplates on one building's door

beats.say: One study put it plainly: 'the easiest method adopted was to multiply the number of units'.
beats.caption: 'multiply the number of units'
beats.visual: Quote card; small credit 'MIDS working paper'

beats.say: In nineteen eighty-four, a business magazine wrote it was 'unlikely that there are more than five hundred families in the business'.
beats.caption: ≈500 families
beats.visual: 500 small family icons

beats.say: Yet official notes from the nineties and the two thousands count about two thousand five hundred knitting units. A few hundred families. Thousands of units.
beats.caption: ≈2,500 knitting units
beats.visual: Family icons each sprout several workshop icons; counter to 2,500

beats.say: Many small units means many small doors in. And that is where the workers come in.
beats.visual: Rows of small doors open

beats.say: There's a local word for it. Kashtakkoottu. A skilled worker teams up with people who have money, and takes a share of the profit. Ten to twenty-five percent.
beats.caption: Kashtakkoottu · 10–25%
beats.visual: Worker + financier icons shake on a split coin

beats.say: And when a unit fails, its machines don't vanish. They're sold second-hand to the next person starting out.
beats.caption: Second-hand machines
beats.visual: One machine passes from a closed shutter to a new one

beats.say: Researchers wrote that almost all the big names in Tiruppur 'have had very humble beginnings, having been workers themselves'.
beats.caption: 'workers themselves'
beats.visual: Quote card; small credit 'MIDS'

beats.say: Who owned the units changed too. One account says owners from the Chettiar community left after strikes in the nineteen sixties, and Gounder owners rose. Other researchers heard a different version. It's disputed.
beats.caption: Disputed
beats.visual: Neutral text card only; no community colours on any map (dossier §8)
beats.ak_check: t45: caste (rule 4.4). Told as a dispute only. AK decides.

beats.say: For decades all this was cottage work: vests and briefs for local shops. Then, from nineteen eighty, the town began selling abroad, mostly through agents in Bombay and Delhi.
beats.caption: From 1980: exports
beats.visual: Arrows from Tiruppur to Bombay and Delhi, then out to sea

beats.say: Until nineteen eighty-five, it exported exactly one thing. The T-shirt.
beats.caption: Only the T-shirt
beats.visual: A single white T-shirt on an empty map

beats.say: Between nineteen eighty-six and nineteen ninety-three, its direct exports grew about thirty-two times in value.
beats.caption: ≈32× · ₹37.48 cr → ₹1,197.5 cr
beats.visual: Bar grows 32× in seven ticks; credit 'TEA table, 1994'

beats.say: The workshops had their own fight. In nineteen eighty-four, banian workers went on strike for a hundred and twenty-seven days, over wages and dearness allowance.
beats.caption: 1984 · 127 days
beats.visual: Calendar pages turn 127 times; no violence imagery

beats.say: The union leader recalls workers being 'harassed, beaten up and sometime even set afire'. That is his account.
beats.visual: Black card, quote only, credit 'K. Subbarayan, 2004'
beats.ak_check: t52: 'set afire' (rule 4.4). One side's recollection; strong image. AK decides.

beats.say: From nineteen eighty-seven, wages were settled for the whole town at once, through a joint committee. In March twenty twenty-six, employers and unions signed the latest town-wide deal.
beats.caption: One wage deal for the town
beats.visual: Six employer badges and nine union badges around one table

beats.say: So that's the first half of the answer. Cotton and yarn next door. A rule that kept units small. And workers who could become owners.
beats.caption: COTTON · SMALL · OWNERS
beats.visual: Cards 1 and 2 face up

beats.say: But small units can't build a port. Or a river.
beats.visual: Card 3 still face down; empty coast, empty riverbed

beats.say: In nineteen ninety-four, the exporters' association asked for an inland container terminal, a sewage plant and a telephone exchange. It wrote that it 'has received no reply from authorities'.
beats.caption: 1994: 'no reply'
beats.visual: Three request letters; no reply arrives

beats.say: So the exporters built an export estate of their own at Mudalipalayam. In ten months. 'Self financed by the exporters'.
beats.caption: 157 units · ₹14 crore
beats.visual: Sheds rise in a time-lapse; credit 'TEA, 1994'

beats.say: Later came a container freight station, about ten kilometres from town, where customs is done locally.
beats.caption: CFS ≈10 km
beats.visual: Container stack near town; customs stamp

beats.say: That's cargo. Now the water. Remember the tankers driving fifty kilometres?
beats.visual: Tanker from b05 returns

beats.say: In Erode district, the Cauvery river meets the Bhavani.
beats.caption: Cauvery + Bhavani
beats.visual: Map zooms to the confluence; place names only

beats.say: So who brought that water to Tiruppur? Take a guess.
beats.caption: Who?
beats.visual: Hold on the confluence and Tiruppur, gap between them

beats.say: A company whose promoters are a Tamil Nadu government body, a finance company called IL&FS, and the exporters' own association.
beats.caption: TWIC · IL&FS · TEA
beats.visual: Three logos as plain text badges join; TEA badge glows amber. Music rises

beats.say: An intake on the Cauvery. A treatment plant nearby. Then a main pipeline, about fifty-three and a half kilometres, to a reservoir at Tiruppur.
beats.caption: ≈53.5 km
beats.visual: Pipeline draws between named places (Anainasuvampalayam → Suriyampalayam → Thiruvachi → Tiruppur); label 'route illustrative'

beats.say: It draws about a hundred and eighty-five million litres a day.
beats.caption: 185 million litres/day
beats.visual: Counter; water fills the pipe

beats.say: The project cost about one thousand and twenty-three crore rupees.
beats.caption: ₹1,023 crore
beats.visual: Coin stack beside the pipe

beats.say: Read that again. A dry town, whose rivers run only in the monsoon, went and fetched one. And its exporters were among the promoters.
beats.caption: A town that fetched a river
beats.visual: Hold on the full pipeline at dusk; card 3 flips: BUILT

beats.say: But bringing water in was half the story. Getting it out clean was the other half.
beats.visual: Pipe reverses: dirty water flows out

beats.say: Dyeing cloth here used two hundred to four hundred litres of water for every kilo. The international norm is about a hundred and twenty to a hundred and fifty.
beats.caption: 200–400 L/kg vs 120–150
beats.visual: Two buckets side by side; credit 'UNIDO'

beats.say: Downstream, a farmers' association on the Noyyal river has fought the polluters in court since two thousand and three.
beats.caption: Farmers in court since 2003
beats.visual: Farm fields downstream; court pillar icon

beats.say: In two thousand and six, the High Court gave the dye houses a deadline. Zero liquid discharge: treat the waste water and release none of it. By July two thousand and seven.
beats.caption: ZLD by 31 Jul 2007
beats.visual: Name the part: ZLD = nothing leaves the plant

beats.say: In early twenty eleven, the court ordered more than seven hundred dyeing and bleaching units and treatment plants shut.
beats.caption: 700+ shut
beats.visual: Shutters come down across the map

beats.say: They reopened about a year and a half later, in June twenty twelve, under zero liquid discharge.
beats.caption: June 2012: reopened
beats.visual: Shutters rise slowly

beats.say: Four hundred and fifty dye units built eighteen shared treatment plants, with money from the Centre too.
beats.caption: 450 units · 18 plants
beats.visual: 18 plant icons; small credit 'Ministry of Textiles, Dec 2016'

beats.say: Today, the Dyers Association says those plants recover ninety-two percent of the water.
beats.caption: 92% (Dyers Association)
beats.visual: Water loop arrow; credit on screen

beats.say: But the same association says more than a lakh tonnes of mixed salt now sit in sheds, and that 'no proper disposal method has been identified so far'.
beats.caption: 1 lakh tonnes of salt
beats.visual: Sheds of white salt; 100,000 counter

beats.say: Back in twenty eleven, D D Basu of the Central Pollution Control Board put it bluntly. 'That is why ZLD at Tirupur was a big mistake.'
beats.caption: 'a big mistake'
beats.visual: Quote card, credit 'D D Basu, CPCB, 2011'

beats.say: Is the river better? One field report saw black water oozing from the floodgates. Years later, an IIT Madras professor spoke of a 'significant improvement'. The evidence is split.
beats.visual: Split screen: two reports, two dates

beats.say: Zoom out again. For twenty twenty-five to twenty-six, the government counted thirty-eight thousand six hundred and seventy-seven crore rupees of textile and clothing exports from Tiruppur.
beats.caption: ₹38,677 crore (DGCIS)
beats.visual: Map pulls back; counter; credit 'DGCIS provisional, via PIB 11 Aug 2026'

beats.say: Where does India's knitted clothing go? About a third of it, by value, goes to the United States.
beats.caption: India knitwear → USA: 32%
beats.visual: Great-circle arc India → USA on the globe; caption 'India, HS 61, 2025'

beats.say: Last year, that market swung hard. For a few months, US duties on Indian goods added up to fifty percent.
beats.caption: 2025: 50% (ended Feb 2026)
beats.visual: Tariff gauge spikes, then drops

beats.say: Today it's a ten percent tariff, on top of the normal duty. And T-shirts are not exempt.
beats.caption: Now: +10% (from 24 Jul 2026)
beats.visual: Gauge settles at 10; a T-shirt icon under it

beats.say: A trade deal with Britain has been in force since July twenty twenty-six. A deal with the European Union is agreed, but not yet in force.
beats.caption: UK: in force · EU: not yet
beats.visual: Arcs to UK (solid) and EU (dashed)

beats.say: So how did a town with no port and little water become India's top exporting district for textiles and clothing? It had cotton coming in, and yarn next door. A rule kept units small, so workers could become owners. And whatever it lacked, an estate, a cargo station, even a river, it built or fetched.
beats.caption: COTTON · SMALL · BUILT
beats.visual: All three cards face up over the map

beats.say: Look at the map one more time. No port for about a hundred and seventy kilometres. Rivers that run only in the monsoon. And a pipeline the town helped build anyway.
beats.visual: Return to the cold-open satellite frame; the pipeline now glows amber

beats.say: Geography gave Tiruppur its cotton. Everything else, it had to make.
beats.visual: Slow push on the town lights; music up; hold 2 s
